newsitem.title: USA: US crudes bolstered by supply reductions in Canada.
newsitem.headline: US crudes bolstered by supply reductions in Canada.

text.p: U.S. cash crude prices held steady Friday, underpinned by gasoline strength on the outright market and planned Canadian exports for September.
Traders said grades were most active for West Texas Sour/Midland where deals trimmed five cents off the differential to September West Texas Intermediate/Cushing.
OIther grades popped slightly higher for Light Louisiana Sweet/St. James and Midland/WTI, before values settled back down to unchanged marks.
Outright crudes ended steady at $20.00-10 a barrel, in the upper half of a narrow trading band. September NYMEX futures settled the final session of the week 1 cts lower at $20.07.

Gasoline supply tightness continued to keep the entire energy complex on firmer footing, despite the start to Iraqi crude exports. Troubles at Exxon's Baytown, Texas and Tosco's Bayway refinery in New Jersey supplied the engine for gasoline upticks, traders said.

On the Iraqi front, another two contracts were approved Friday by U.N. overseers, both for Russian companies, bringing the total for approved contracts to 18 and the volume count to more than 90 million barrels.
Reports also said U.S. trader Bayoil's tanker Arcadia departed the Turkish port of Ceyhan loaded with more than 2 million barrels of Iraqi crude for the U.S. Gulf.

In the grade universe, domestic barrels found firmer bids for sour parcels off news of a supply cut for Canadian oil. The IPL Energy Inc's Interprovincial Pipe Line, which brings crude from western Canada to the U.S. Midwest, announced it expected to cut September throughputs some 141,000 barrels per day (bpd). Maintenance forced the cuts from the normal 1.5 million bpd level.
That news pushed WTS/Midland to talk late at WTI -$1.28/25, trading as strong as $1.25 under benchmark.
Traders pegged Light Louisiana Sweet/St. James at a 23/24 cents premium to September WTI, around the same levels recorded Thursday.
Postings Plus steadied at $1.87/90, working off a steady September/October roll of -21 cents.
